passage:
Subject: A plan so you can rest

Dear Devika,

Last night I saw you fall asleep at Amma's bedside with the phone in your hand. I have been thinking about it all day. For two months you have done every night and every visit, and I let it happen because you never complained. That was wrong of me.

One person cannot hold this up for the long run, so here is a plan. You take nights on Monday, Wednesday and Friday. I take the other nights and weekends. We hire a helper from ten to two on weekdays. And Thursday is your day off, no phone.

If it does not work, we change it. But please say yes.

Jasleen

qa.q: Which day is Devika's day off?
How does Jasleen feel about the past two months?
qa.a: Jasleen feels guilty and worried, admitting that letting Devika carry everything was wrong.

qa.q: What could Jasleen and Devika do if the hired helper does not suit Amma?
qa.a: They could try a different helper or change the hours, and adjust the rest of the schedule so nobody is overloaded.

qa.q: How might Devika feel reading the email?
qa.a: Devika may feel relief at the offer of rest but also some reluctance to let go, since Devika has held the whole load for two months.

grounding: The email shows a person who realises one sibling cannot carry everything and plans rest shifts, paid help for some hours and a day off.
